title: Wind Farms: Power from the Air
summary: How wind turbines turn moving air into electricity, why wind farms are a clean source of power with some challenges, and how Saudi Arabia has begun using wind energy at Dumat Al Jandal.
poll: Every country should build more wind farms.

versions.title: Power from the Wind
versions.text:
Feel the wind on your face. Wind is air that moves. It can push hard.

Long ago, people used wind to grind grain. They built mills with big arms. The wind spun the arms.

Now we use wind to make power. We use a tall tower. On top are three long blades. The whole thing is a turbine.

The wind pushes the blades. The blades spin. A machine at the top turns the spin into power. The power goes out on wires. It goes to homes. It lights lamps. It runs fans.

A wind farm has lots of turbines. They stand where the wind is strong. Some stand in the sea.

Wind power is clean. It does not make smoke. And the wind will not run out.

But the wind does not blow all the time. When it stops, the blades stop, too. So we need more kinds of power, too.

Saudi Arabia has a big wind farm. It is in the north. Its name is Dumat Al Jandal.

versions.title: Wind Farms: Turning Air into Electricity
versions.text:
Stand outside on a windy day, and you can feel the air push against you. Wind is simply moving air, but it carries a lot of energy.

People have used wind for a very long time. More than a thousand years ago, people in Persia built windmills to grind grain. Later, windmills also pumped water for farms.

Today, we use the wind to make electricity. A modern wind turbine has a tall tower with three long blades on top. Some turbines are taller than a building with thirty floors.

When the wind blows, it pushes the blades and makes them spin. The blades turn a shaft connected to a generator, which changes the spinning motion into electricity. Cables then carry the electricity to the power grid, a network of wires that brings power to homes, schools, and factories.

A wind farm is a large group of turbines. Wind farms are built where the wind is strong and steady, such as plains, hills, and coasts. Some are built out at sea.

Wind is a renewable source of energy because it will never run out. It is also clean. Turbines do not burn fuel, so they do not cause air pollution.

However, wind power has a problem. The wind does not always blow, so the amount of electricity changes from hour to hour. That is why wind farms must work together with other power sources.

Saudi Arabia opened its first large wind farm at Dumat Al Jandal, in the north of the Kingdom. It has nearly one hundred turbines.

versions.title: Wind Farms: Turning Air into Electricity
versions.text:
Stand outside on a windy day, and you can feel the air pushing against you. Wind is simply moving air, but it carries a surprising amount of energy.

Humans have harnessed the wind for centuries. More than a thousand years ago, people in Persia constructed windmills to grind grain, and eventually, windmills also pumped water for agricultural villages.

Today, engineers use the wind to generate electricity. A modern wind turbine consists of a tall tower with three enormous blades mounted on top, and some turbines are taller than a building with thirty floors.

When the wind blows, it pushes against the blades and causes them to rotate. The blades turn a shaft connected to a generator, which converts the rotating motion into electricity. Cables then transmit the electricity to the power grid, an enormous network of wires that delivers energy to homes, schools, and factories.

A wind farm is a large collection of turbines, and engineers construct wind farms in locations where the wind is powerful and consistent, such as open plains, hilltops, and coastlines. Some are even installed out at sea.

Wind is a renewable source of energy because it will never be used up. It is also clean, since turbines do not burn fuel and therefore do not produce air pollution.

However, wind power has one significant limitation. The wind does not blow continuously, so the amount of electricity varies from hour to hour. For this reason, wind farms must operate alongside other energy sources.

Saudi Arabia opened its first large wind farm at Dumat Al Jandal, in the northern region of the Kingdom. The facility contains nearly one hundred turbines, which together can supply electricity to many thousands of households.

versions.title: Harvesting the Wind: How Wind Farms Make Electricity
versions.text:
Stand outside on a blustery day, and you can feel the air pushing against you. Wind is simply moving air, created when the sun heats different regions of the Earth unevenly, and it carries a surprising amount of energy.

Humans have harnessed the wind for centuries. More than a thousand years ago, people in Persia constructed windmills to grind grain, and eventually, windmills also pumped water for agricultural communities.

Today, engineers use the wind to generate electricity. A modern wind turbine consists of a tall tower with three enormous blades mounted on top, and many turbines are taller than a building with thirty floors.

Moving air possesses kinetic energy, the energy of motion. When the wind blows, it pushes against the blades and causes them to rotate, and the blades turn a shaft connected to a generator, which converts the rotating motion into electricity. Cables then transmit the electricity to the power grid, which distributes it to residences and industries.

A wind farm is a large collection of turbines. Engineers construct wind farms in locations where the wind is powerful and consistent, such as open plains and coastlines. Offshore wind farms are installed at sea, where winds are frequently stronger and steadier than on land.

Wind is renewable because it will never be used up, and it is environmentally clean, since turbines release no emissions of smoke or harmful gases while they operate. Nevertheless, engineers study the migration routes of birds before choosing a location, because rotating blades can occasionally injure flying animals.

However, wind power is intermittent, meaning its output rises and falls. Because the wind does not blow continuously, the quantity of electricity varies from hour to hour. Consequently, wind farms must operate alongside other energy sources or large batteries.

Saudi Arabia opened its first large wind farm at Dumat Al Jandal, in the northern region of the Kingdom. Its nearly one hundred turbines are part of the country's plan to build a more sustainable energy future.

Saudi Arabia inaugurated its first utility-scale wind farm at Dumat Al Jandal, in the northern region of the Kingdom. Its nearly one hundred turbines represent part of the nation's strategy to develop a more sustainable energy future.

versions.title: Harvesting the Wind: The Science of Wind Farms
versions.text:
Stand outside on a blustery day, and you can feel the air pushing against you. Wind is simply moving air, generated when the sun heats different regions of the Earth unevenly, and it carries a remarkable quantity of energy.

Humans have harnessed the wind for centuries. More than a thousand years ago, people in Persia constructed windmills to grind grain, and eventually, windmills also pumped water for agricultural communities across several continents.

Today, engineers use the wind to generate electricity. A modern wind turbine consists of a tall tower with three enormous blades mounted on top, and many turbines are taller than a building with thirty floors.

Moving air possesses kinetic energy, the energy of motion. When the wind blows, it pushes against the aerodynamically designed blades and causes them to rotate, and the blades turn a shaft connected to a generator, which converts the rotational motion into electricity. Cables subsequently transmit the electricity to the power grid, which distributes it to residences and industries throughout the region.

A wind farm is an extensive collection of turbines. Engineers construct wind farms in locations where the wind is powerful and consistent, such as open plains and coastlines. Offshore wind farms are installed at sea, where winds are frequently stronger and more reliable than on land, although constructing and maintaining them is considerably more expensive.

Wind is renewable because it will never be exhausted, and it is environmentally clean, since turbines release no emissions of smoke or harmful gases while they operate. Nevertheless, engineers carefully investigate the migration routes of birds before selecting a location, because rotating blades can occasionally injure flying animals.

However, wind power is intermittent, meaning its output rises and falls unpredictably. Because the wind does not blow continuously, the quantity of electricity fluctuates from hour to hour, and consequently, wind farms must operate in combination with other energy sources or large-scale batteries that store surplus electricity.

Saudi Arabia inaugurated its first utility-scale wind farm at Dumat Al Jandal, in the northern region of the Kingdom. Its nearly one hundred turbines represent part of the nation's ambitious strategy to develop a more sustainable and diversified energy future.

Humans have harnessed the wind for centuries: more than a thousand years ago, people in Persia constructed windmills to grind grain, and eventually, windmills also pumped water for agricultural communities across several continents.

Cables subsequently transmit the electricity to the power grid, which distributes it to residences and industries throughout the region.

A wind farm is an extensive collection of turbines, which engineers construct in locations where the wind is powerful and consistent, such as open plains and coastlines. Offshore wind farms are installed at sea, where winds are frequently stronger and more reliable than on land, although constructing and maintaining them in corrosive saltwater environments is considerably more expensive.

HIGH.prompt: A town council must decide whether to build a wind farm or a new power plant that burns fuel. Write a recommendation using evidence from the article, including at least one challenge of wind power.
checklist: I supported it with at least three pieces of evidence, including a challenge.
I used academic words such as intermittent, emissions, or sustainable.
HIGH.modelAnswer: I recommend that the town council build the wind farm instead of a power plant that burns fuel. Wind turbines use kinetic energy from moving air to spin a generator, producing clean electricity without emissions or air pollution, unlike a fuel-burning plant. Wind is also a renewable, sustainable resource, since it will never run out, and some wind farms can even be built offshore where the wind blows steadily. The main challenge is that wind power is intermittent, because the wind does not always blow at the same strength, so the town would need another power source to use alongside it during calm periods. Even with this challenge, the environmental benefits make the wind farm the better long-term choice.
